prompt: A production docker-compose file references `myapp:latest` with `pull_policy: always`. An autoscaling event at 2 AM pulls a broken image with no deploy event logged anywhere. What actually caused this?
choices: The autoscaler pulled whatever `latest` currently pointed to, which a routine CI build had silently repointed to a broken image hours earlier
Docker Hub corrupted the image during storage
The autoscaler ignored the pull policy and used a cached broken layer
git-SHA tags expired and Docker fell back to latest automatically

prompt: Which tag should a production deploy manifest actually reference to get an unambiguous, auditable rollback target?
choices: latest
A semver tag like 1.4.2, since it is never reused
A git-SHA tag, since exactly one commit maps to exactly one image
Whichever tag was pushed most recently

prompt: In a Dockerfile with `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` followed by `RUN npm ci` followed by `COPY . .`, why does editing only a source file (not package.json) leave `RUN npm ci` cached on rebuild?
choices: Docker always caches RUN instructions regardless of changes
npm itself detects that no dependencies changed and skips the install
The COPY step that feeds npm ci only checksums package.json and package-lock.json, which didn't change, so that layer and everything depending on it up to that point stays a cache hit
The source file edit happened after the build started, so Docker ignores it

prompt: If a Dockerfile layer gets a cache miss, what happens to every layer defined after it?
choices: They are unaffected as long as their own instructions didn't change
They must all be rebuilt too, because each layer is a diff applied on top of the filesystem state the previous layer produced
Docker skips them and reuses the previous image's final layer instead
Only the very next layer rebuilds; the rest stay cached

prompt: When authenticating to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) with `docker login ghcr.io`, what should you use in place of your GitHub account password?
choices: Your GitHub password works directly and is recommended
A personal access token with the write:packages scope (or the GITHUB_TOKEN injected automatically in GitHub Actions)
Your SSH private key
A Docker Hub access token, since GHCR and Docker Hub share credentials

prompt: A Dockerfile does `COPY .env .` then later `RUN rm .env` to "clean up" before the final image. Why does the secret remain recoverable by anyone who pulls the image?
choices: It doesn't remain recoverable; rm permanently erases it from the image

Each instruction produces its own layer tarball; rm in a later layer only hides the file at runtime with a whiteout marker, while the earlier layer's tarball containing .env is still pushed and pullable
Docker automatically re-adds deleted files on push for integrity checking
The secret is only recoverable if the image is tagged latest

prompt: What is the correct way to supply a one-time secret (like a private package registry token) needed only during an image build, without it ending up baked into a layer?
choices: COPY the secret file in, use it, then RUN rm it in a later instruction
Set it with ENV so it's available but not copied as a file
Use BuildKit's mount-based secret (RUN --mount=type=secret) so it's available to the build step but never written into a layer
Pass it as a build ARG, since ARG values are never stored in the image
